candidate.name: Remove redundant hidden-output clears before overwrite-only projections
candidate.minimal_change: Delete only the two std::fill(h_.begin(), h_.end(), 0.0f) calls immediately before attention-output and FFN-down matvec in Model::step(). No changes to logits allocation, buffers, backend API, arithmetic, scheduling, or batched forward.
candidate.current_cost: Each clear writes n_embd floats on the calling thread before projection workers overwrite the same complete output. Total source-level redundant stores are 8*n_layer*n_embd bytes per step. Compiler retention and material latency cost have not been measured; no speedup estimate is justified.
exactness_basis: Backend::matmul specifies assignment Y[b*nout+o] = dot(...), not accumulation.
CPU Q8 matvec, Q4_K single-row path, F32 path, and general dequantized path assign every successful output.
Model::forward_batch already invokes these projections without clearing hb_ first.
tests/backend_group.cpp seeds output buffers with 123456 and compares them against independent double dots; existing tests exercise overwrite semantics.
limits: The model already wrote h_ during normalization, so removing clears does not eliminate all caller-to-worker cache ownership traffic.
An exception can leave different partial scratch contents, but the runtime does not promise recovery of a partially executed model session. Do not weaken existing backend error guarantees.
Small redundant-store volume and historical matrix-dominated measurements make a material gain uncertain; no current profiling attributes time to these clears.
candidate.not_duplicate: Commit 46570b0 preallocated gate/up/ffn and attention scores but retained these exact h_ clears. This candidate changes neither allocation nor prefetch, Q8 pairing, packed activations, pointer increments, explicit inlining, worker polling, caller invocation, or kernel reduction order.
gates: Before any expensive run, inspect ordinary control/candidate MSVC and GCC emitted step code to confirm both store loops exist and disappear. Stop as a compiler-null experiment if they already vanish.
Build both compilers and run unchanged native 7-test suites and full required-HF Python suites; retain all thresholds.

Compare raw finite F32/Q8 logits with unchanged control over prefill plus forced continuation and all existing NLL cases; require bit identity and zero added NLL, plus independent HF bounds. Include 8B pinned HF gate, follow-up chat, one-token prefill and batch tails.

Only after correctness and activation evidence, run fixed predeclared alternating control/candidate/mx comparison on 0.6B and 8B with identical tokens, quants, hardware, threads, ubatch and F32 KV. Discard only planned warmup, retain every sample, report mean/median/range/paired wins; no overlapping workloads and no early favorable stopping.
Run required tests/perf.py and record before/after; do not confuse repeated-step synthetic prefill with true batched prefill. A null result must not be claimed as a performance fix.
candidate.recommendation: Low priority. This is the only proposed change from this review. If the current epilogue study is null, the existing evidence supports no immediate high-confidence exact optimization; do not launch another broad speculative kernel sweep.
